core: shape as a two-dimensional bounded area
outOfScope: attributing private intention from formal features alone

claims.claim: Shape is two-dimensional, with height and width, while form has height, width, and depth.
A shape may be defined by a contour or by a visible edge between areas rather than only by a drawn outline.
Geometric shapes are regular or mathematically named, while organic or biomorphic shapes are commonly irregular, curving, or associated with living forms.
The areas around and between figures can be analyzed as negative space or negative shapes in relationship to occupied figures.
Formal analysis can begin with close description of visual features and should be combined with other methods when questions exceed what visual evidence alone can establish.
A three-dimensional object can remain a form while presenting different flat outlines and visible arrangements from different viewpoints.
